case.description: One case: what it is called, what it is given, and what every runtime has to answer.

expected.description: What every runtime has to answer.

input.description: What the capability is given. screens.admit takes document. screens.resolve takes document and root, and screen where only one screen is resolved. screens.validate_screen takes document and screen, and - rather than a root key - responses, and context where the case supplies one, at the top level: the two together are the root the screen is validated against, the same one the host resolved with, and a half the case leaves out is read as an empty map, so a path into it is undecidable like any other path the root lacks. It also takes pressed_button where a button was pressed. screens.seal_secrets takes document, screen and responses, the responses an object keyed by question key, and seals with the one test sealer every runtime supplies: it counts the plaintexts it is handed within one call, from 1, and for the n-th gives back an error where the plaintext begins SEALER-REFUSES, the number n rather than a string where it begins SEALER-GIVES-NUMBER, and the sealed string test-sealed-n otherwise, so a case states how many times, and in what order, the sealer is applied. templates.render takes source, and assigns and mode where the case renders; mode is lenient, strict, or both, and both means the case is run in each mode and both runs have to give the stated answer. journey.present takes document, root and status, and screen where the status is a screen, opts where a screen status carries them, info where a waiting status carries one, and result where a done status carries one: status is screen, waiting or done, screen names the key a screen status asks for, opts is the map a screen status carries and may be any JSON value, a map or not, info is the map a waiting status carries and may be any JSON value, a map or not, result is the map a done status carries and may likewise be any JSON value, and any other status is a status outside the three. journey.put_context takes root and context, and context may be any JSON value, a map or not. journey.decode_submit takes submit, which may be any JSON value, an object or not. journey.from_data takes data, the data form a host keeps for a Journey's scope, which may be any JSON value, an object or not. journey.check takes access, actor, scope and operation, and is run against the three fixed test access modules every runtime supplies, by the name access gives: members, whose member? is true when the actor is an array holding the scope's data form, kind and id and no other key, and false otherwise, and whose scopes lists the items of the actor that are such a data form, in order, and is empty when the actor is not an array; present_only, whose member? and scopes are those of members, and which exports allowed?, true for the operation present and false otherwise; and not_boolean, whose member? gives back the string true for every actor and scope. Any other access is handed over as itself, which is not a module exporting member?. actor may be any JSON value and is handed over as it is. scope is handed over as the scope journey.from_data reads it to where that reads it, and as the case states it otherwise. operation is present, submit or back, and any other value is handed over as itself, which is an operation outside the three. journey.check_kind takes scope and expected_kind: scope is handed over as journey.check hands it over, and expected_kind, the one scope kind the host's Path record names, may be any JSON value, a string or not.

name.description: The rule the case pins, in prose. A case that fails is read by its name before it is read by its data.

description: One capability's conformance cases. A case is an input and the answer every runtime has to give for it, so a runtime in a second language is held to the same behavior as the reference one. Two conventions hold across every file. A finding in an expected answer carries code, field and element_key and no message: the code is the stable thing a host switches on and the message is prose a second runtime is not obliged to reproduce word for word. And the author writes name, capability and cases; the export task that copies these files out of this repository adds its own provenance header beside them, which is why this schema does not forbid further keys at the top level.

capability.description: The behavior every case in the file exercises. screens.admit runs the input document through admission and reports whether it is a document and every finding against it. screens.resolve resolves a document against a root, or one named screen of it. screens.validate_screen resolves the named screen against the same root the host resolved with and reports what the responses in it have to satisfy. screens.seal_secrets seals the responses to the named screen's secret questions with the fixed test sealer and states ok, and beside it the responses as sealed or the findings against them, or an error stated as error and its reason. templates.render compiles template source against the subset and, where the case names a mode, renders it. journey.present presents the status a host passes as a screen, waiting or done; a screen is resolved against the root and carries the diagnostics of resolving it, with the moves the screen allows beside it and the progress the host supplied beside them where it supplied one, and an error is stated as error and its reason. journey.put_context gives back the root with its context replaced whole, or an error stated the same way. journey.decode_submit decodes the submit or the back request a client sends back and states ok, and beside it, under submit, the submit or the back request as decoded, or the findings against it. journey.from_data reads the data form a host keeps for a Journey's scope back into a scope and states ok, and beside it, under scope, the scope's data form, kind and id, or an error stated as error and its reason. journey.check asks whether an actor may take an operation in the Journey of a scope, of one of the fixed test access modules, and states ok, or an error stated as error and its reason, the same reason whatever the cause. journey.check_kind compares a scope's kind with the kind a Path expects, byte for byte, and states ok or an error stated the same way.

generated_by.description: Written by the export task when it copies the file out: the word riddler, a space, the word from, a space and the file's path in the repository it was authored in, as in "riddler from corpus/screens/admit.json". It names no version, no timestamp and no commit. An authored file does not carry it.
